## Context

Establish the nested `rebar bridge` CLI through a shippable vertical slice. The parent story originally proposed advertising all eight final verbs before their owning stories implemented them. That would expose broken placeholders on `main`. This task therefore registers only the two verbs it owns now: `preview` and `sync`. Later dependency-ordered stories extend the group only when each handler is functional.

`preview` is the read-only path over the existing reconciler dry-run mode. `sync` is the mutating path over the existing live mode. The legacy top-level `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` spellings remain unchanged at this boundary.

## Approach

- Add `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` as the nested-group parser and shared reconciler subprocess launcher.
- Keep `_cli._reconcile` as a compatibility wrapper around that launcher until story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` retires the top-level verb.
- Route the help-backed `bridge` noun from `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`.
- Register only `preview` and `sync`: preview forces `dry-run`; sync forces `live`.
- Reject `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and arbitrary trailing arguments so callers cannot override the read/write distinction. The public `--max-changes`, `--only`, `--except`, and `--max-age` flags do not exist yet; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` will add them together with their behavior and migration.
- Define exact discovery contracts: no nested verb prints group usage; `--help` prints usage; an unknown nested verb fails with the valid choices and never falls through to a same-named top-level command.
- Update `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md`, add the new dispatcher arms and exit contracts to `docs/exit-codes.md`, and document only the staged surface that actually ships.
- Preserve `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, the `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` round trip, top-level `doctor`, and all legacy bridge spellings.

## Surface parity

- CLI: in scope and exercised through the real `rebar` entrypoint.
- Library and MCP: out of scope; story `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` owns those surfaces.
- Automated workflows and scripts: out of scope; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` owns their migration.
- Dual direction: both preview/read and sync/write are proven here.

## Testing

Use a real CLI subprocess against a temporary git-backed tracker plus a stateful fake Jira transport built from production-shaped fixtures. A unit-only dispatch test is insufficient because parsing, subprocess wiring, mode selection, and persisted state are contractual.

RED-first oracle:
- happy path: `rebar bridge preview` returns the real reconciler JSON plan;
- held out: exact before/after snapshots prove preview performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes;
- held out: sync starts from an unbound remote-only issue, creates the real local/binding mutation, and preserves unrelated event bytes;
- held out: no-verb, help, unknown verb, top-level-name collision, forbidden flag, phase-gate, doctor, legacy-command, generated-reference, and exit-code-table contracts;
- mutation: routing preview to live must fail the no-write oracle; routing sync to dry-run must fail the persisted-mutation oracle.

This wrapper adds no new composed store operation, retry loop, or cache, so the shared contention suites remain the responsibility of the reconciler core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge`, `rebar bridge --help`, `rebar bridge preview --help`, and `rebar bridge sync --help` expose only functional `preview` and `sync` verbs with pinned exit/stream contracts.
- [ ] An unknown nested verb fails with valid choices and never dispatches a same-named top-level command.
- [ ] `bridge preview` performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes, proven by exact snapshots and the fake transport log.
- [ ] `bridge sync` performs a persisted mutation from a production-shaped fake Jira fixture while preserving unrelated state.
- [ ] `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and unknown arguments are rejected on both verbs.
- [ ] Help text contains none of the prohibited internal vocabulary from the parent story.
- [ ] `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` remain intact and exercised.
- [ ] Top-level `doctor`, `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` generates the nested group, and `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, and `docs/release-notes.md` describe only the staged surface that ships.
- [ ] Focused pytest nodes, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Rollback

This is additive and changes no persisted schema. Revert the single Gerrit change to remove the nested group while leaving every legacy spelling intact.
